reasoning: The package contains standard AUR packaging for omnisharp-roslyn. The PKGBUILD sources from the official upstream GitHub repository pinned to tag v1.40.0 with a SHA256 checksum. The prepare(), build(), and package() functions contain only routine .NET build customizations (sed edits for system dotnet, telemetry opt-out, standard artifact installation). No malicious patterns (eval, curl|bash, obfuscation, unexpected network endpoints) were found. The two inconclusive results were caused by tool errors (API HTTP 400 error on .gitignore, JSONDecodeError), not security concerns. The deepseek model provided thorough analysis confirming all files are safe.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool errors, not security findings. Report 1 (qwen) failed on .gitignore due to HTTP 400 API error, and Report 3 (openrouter, advisory-only) failed on PKGBUILD due to JSONDecodeError. Report 2 (deepseek) successfully reviewed all files and found no issues. The inconclusive verdicts were artifacts of infrastructure failures, not evidence of risk.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen): .gitignore review failed due to HTTP 400 API error
Report 3 (openrouter): PKGBUILD review failed due to JSONDecodeError, and only 1 of 3 files was reviewed
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, JSON parsing errors) on non-executable files like .gitignore should not force an inconclusive verdict when other critical files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO) are successfully reviewed and found safe
The audit tool should distinguish between 'file could not be analyzed due to tool error' and 'file contains suspicious content' when computing final verdicts
Advisory reports that fail due to tool errors should be excluded from verdict calculation entirely, not just marked as non-voting
